name: Hushim
overview: Hushim is a female member of the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the wife of Shaharaim. Her identity is grounded in her marital relationship within the genealogical records of Israel. There are no additional notes or distinguishing attributes recorded about her in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: Hushim is the only recorded name for this individual, and no specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to it in the biblical text. It is simply presented as a proper name in 1 Chronicles 8:8.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hushim as the wife of Shaharaim. Additionally, Shaharaim is noted as the father of Abitub and Elpaal, which situates Hushim within this family line. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Hushim's significance lies in her inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, highlighting the faithfulness of God's covenant people through their family lines. Her mention as the wife of Shaharaim connects her to the lineage that preserves the heritage of Israel. Although brief, her presence in 1 Chronicles underscores the importance of family and tribal identity in the biblical narrative.
